title: Grewingk Lake topobathy, first attempt (ice as of 19 Sep 2023), 2 m
note: First Grewingk Lake topobathy, Hig's request of 2026-10-13: the lake bed from the levelled 2023 multibeam (grewingk_sonar_2023) where it exists, everything else in the lake from the fill's lake basin conditioned by every sounding (Ed Berg's 2017 sounder track, Hig's lead-line drops 2017/2019/2021/2026), the shores from Grewingk 2021 lidar, and the GLACIER as Mark Laker's SfM of 19 September 2023 shows it (dixon_2023; ice = the 2020 G10040 outline minus what the lake had taken by 2023, make_ice.py). Hig's two rules: the ICE FACE is vertical and puts no constraint on the depth (fill: ice_face 'free' -- no shore taper, no fixed value, the basin runs into the face), and the bed is 150 m deep in the middle of the lake (fill: lake_dmax 150 m for the Grewingk Lake domain, in place of the Hollister / glacial-scaling estimate). Lower bounds (lines that ran out) are not used yet. as_of = the SfM date.

layers.name: ctx3dep
layers.notes: Fallback everywhere: USGS 3DEP 1/3 arc-second seamless (~10 m; IfSAR-derived in Alaska), the same data Mapterhorn serves in Alaska (median difference 0 m against this bake, reference_mapterhorn) -- read locally rather than from Mapterhorn's tiles. NAVD88. Date a nominal 2012 (IfSAR era); sigma 3 m, so any survey outranks it and it shows only where nothing else does. Its lakes are hydroflattened: class ground here, so where it is the only data a lake reads as a flat surface -- the class axis from the surveys above still says water there.
layers.class_notes: Stands in only where no survey of the stack has a cell (no footprint rasters: the 2021 class raster is ~60% void over this box). WATER where 3DEP is hydroflattened (flat_water.py: 3x3 range < 1 cm, >= 5000 m2) -- 2026-10-14, so a lake where 3DEP is the only data (Emerald Lake) gets a basin rather than a flat floor.

layers.name: sfm2023bare
layers.notes: Hig 2026-10-14: beyond the 2021 lidar the 2023 SfM (dixon_2023) rather than 3DEP. It is a DSM, so only where it is BARE (dsm_bare.py: its 30 m median < 1 m above 3DEP; canopy left to 3DEP below), levelled to the shifted 2021 lidar by one constant on the bare overlap (sfm_bare_2023.json), never over lakes, ice or the retreat zone, and kept on a 60 m band inside the lidar edge so the lidar's feather blends into it. sigma 1.0: the lidar (0.15) outranks it wherever both exist.

layers.name: kbay2023
layers.notes: Hig 2026-10-14: the NOAA 2023/24 Kachemak Bay lidar (our reclass v2, the published kbay_2023_reclass_v2) over the SW half of the box, and where the two lidars differ the LOWER surface wins. It is below grewingk2021 in the stack and 2021 has the opt-in `lowest` rule: where both exist 2023 stands (newer, same sigma), unless 2021 is lower by > 0.3 m over 50 m. On ground they agree (median -0.05 m, p5/p95 -0.84/+0.69, after the 2021 +0.36 shift), but 2021 stands > 1 m high on 4 %: bad low-density 2021 returns 11-13 m high at 59.62226,-151.18886 and in a 2021 data hole at 59.58333,-151.11495, which the v5 fill had made a pond. No shift: KBay is the datum the others were tied to. Classes: its own point classes where obs/kbay_2023_pts covers, and the 2021 lake / 2023 retreat as water (the reclass fills return-free water from its rim).
layers.class_notes: obs/kbay_2023_pts covers x 595-606 km, y 6602-6610 km only; elsewhere ground unless in the Grewingk lake masks.

layers.name: grewingk2021
layers.notes: shift_m +0.36: MEASURED 2026-10-10, not from metadata. On bare smooth flat ground (both DTMs < 0.05 m rough, slope < 3 deg, 2-20 m: beaches, flats, fans) KBay 2023 reads +0.36 m above Grewingk 2021 with NMAD 0.06 m (n 108k at 2 m), while KBay reads +0.014 m (NMAD 0.048) against Seldovia 2019 NCMP topobathy, the survey the 2009 bathymetry's MLLW->NAVD88 shift was tied to, and the reclass matches the vendor DEM to 1 cm. Two independent products against one: Grewingk sits ~0.36 m low in the collection's NAVD88(GEOID12B) frame despite its metadata. No third witness overlaps it (Homer 2019 and Lower Kenai have no data over it). Belongs in datasets.json as vertical_shift_m for hosting to apply after its own check; applied here explicitly so the test composite has no 0.4 m seam at Grewingk's edge.
layers.class_notes: Ground wherever the DGGS DTM has a value, WATER where the 2021 point classification says so (obs/grewingk_2021_lakes, which is ~60% void over this box, so only its water is used), ICE inside the 2020 glacier outline. DTM cells over the lake that the point classes miss read ground at the water level; the fill drops lake observations within lake_surface_tol_m of the level as surface, not evidence. WATER also wherever the DTM is the flat lake surface (48.55 +- 0.35 m, connected to the point-class lake; make_ice.py lake_2021.tif): without it the lake surface read ground along the ice face, and the fill saw a shore at water level between the lake and the ice. In the retreat zone (lake by 2023, ice in the 2020 outline) the 2021 ice surface is classed WATER: classed ice it still won there under a water class_now (sequential rules), standing the old ice in for the lake bed. ISLANDS (2026-10-14): water-classed returns standing > 0.65 m above the flat lake surface in components >= 50 m2 (make_nohf_dtm.py islands_2021.tif) are GROUND, last so neither the lake masks nor the islets rule take them back. 2026-10-14: the point classes rebuilt over the whole box with every tile on disk (observe_points.py stats/classify -> obs/grewingk_2021_box); the first (2026-10-11) predated the tiles north of y 6610.5 km, and its 'no returns + flat DTM = water' turned the outwash gravels there into ponds (Hig). classify now voids the footprints of unfetched tiles.
layers.source_notes: 2026-10-14 (Hig): the delivered DGGS DTM hydroflattens the lake and with it a real island (59.60571,-151.11924). Rebuilt from the classified points (ground + water returns, mean per 1 m cell, delivered DTM where no return) by make_nohf_dtm.py; was the dataset grewingk_2021.

layers.name: sonar2023
layers.shift_notes: Hig 2026-10-14: the whole topobathy raised 0.36 m to the other DEMs (Grewingk 2021 reads 0.36 m low against KBay 2023 and Seldovia 2019). The multibeam agrees with Ed Berg's sound-corrected track, whose level is tied to the UNSHIFTED 2021 lidar, to 0.2 m -- so it is in that datum and takes the same shift.

layers.name: dixon2023
layers.notes: Mark Laker's SfM DSM (USFWS, dixon_2023), 19 Sep 2023, NAVD88 converted, read from make_ice.py's copy that holds ONLY the 2023 ice and the retreat zone (the lake gained from the 2020 outline): ICE on the tongue, WATER in the retreat zone. Nowhere else -- SfM is poor over water and at the lake shore (Hig, 2026-10-13; here NMAD 2.9 m over the lake, +3.4 m above the lidar on land beside it), and given everywhere it became the newest class over the lake.

layers.name: fill
layers.notes: The hole interpolation (composite.py fill, topobathy/fill.py): a context-aware prior (shore bands from the rim slope, low-tide floor) conditioned by the soundings. Class modelled, so it stands in at half rank under water/bed and never where a real observation exists; sigma from fill_sigma.tif (grows from the shore, relaxes near soundings). Optional: skipped until the fill has been run; 'composite.py fill' treats the cells it won as holes, so build -> fill -> build is idempotent.

lake_dmax.why: Hig 2026-10-13: 150 m deep in the middle of the lake
lake_dmax.level_why: the 12 Oct 2021 lidar water surface (flat at 48.55 m). The 2023 SfM water reads 51.6 m median but scatters NMAD 2.9 m (p5-p95 48-58 m) and stands +3.4 m above the lidar even on land near the lake: not a level. Raised 0.36 m to 48.91 with the 2021 lidar's shift (Hig 2026-10-14).

lake_dmax.why: Emerald Lake (Hig 2026-10-14): the NAU sounder data (Emerald_Bathy_Merged.csv, 3,317 points, via Ed Berg 2017) is likely corrupted, so it does NOT condition the bed: used only for the deepest depth (51.6 m) and the hypsometry -- depths at area fractions 0, 0.05 .. 1 of the lake, each 3DEP lake cell taking the median depth of the nearest 10 m sounding cell (tracks ~60 m apart; 92 % of the lake within 60 m of one), shore set to 0.

fill.notes: Sparse depths: a dated export of the soundings database (Grewingk: Berg 2017 sounder, thinned, level tied to the 2021 lidar (50.05 m), its 2017 ice-face run as lower bounds; Higman lead line 2017/2019/2021/2026; z = each survey's level - depth). ice_face 'free': rim cells classed ice are neither shore (no slope extension, no taper of the basin) nor fixed boundary values (residual and spline free there). lake_dmax: the basin's deepest point fixed by Hig instead of estimated.
fill.channel_notes: Channel detection off for this box (channel_min_m2 huge): it read the deep east end of Grewingk Lake, by the ice face, as a river channel and gave it a shallow channel bed (first fill, 2026-10-13).
fill.shore_grad_notes: Hig 2026-10-14: the measured gradients off a shore inform the assumed one. Each depth within 200 m of shore (soundings, multibeam bed) gives rho = measured / prior depth; log rho smoothed along the lake (sigma 150 m, 3 sites' weight on rho = 1) rescales the basin prior within 200 m of shore, fading out by 400 m. Made for the outlet bay, where the lake-wide shape put a 48 m hole between the cross-outlet sounding line and the river. 2026-10-14 (Hig): the window widens with distance from shore -- local at the water's edge, an ever broader stretch of shore farther out (sigma ~ distance, 150 m to 2.4 km) -- so a few soundings by one cliff no longer set the bed far below it; the same for the land rim slope in the shore band (rim_widen).
fill.points_dz_notes: Every Grewingk sounding level is tied to the UNSHIFTED 2021 lidar (48.55 m water; Ed's level to its dry ground), as the soundings database keeps them (the published grewingk_2021 is unshifted too); the composite raises them with the lidar layer's shift_m (Hig 2026-10-14).

rules_post_notes: feather 15 -> 30 m (2026-10-14, Hig: no feathering where the 2021 lidar drops off -- the feather had nothing underneath to blend with until composite.post_masks laid the nearest lower layer under a partial edge; 30 m because 3DEP and the lidar differ by +-3.5 m (p10/p90) on stable ground).
lowest_notes: Hig 2026-10-14: lower surfaces take priority between the 2021 and 2023 lidar, especially where they differ widely (bad high 2021 returns). grewingk2021 is above kbay2023, so where both exist it takes only where lower by > tol over smooth_m.
